title: Session Catalog — lab notes
body:
Purpose:
- Capture a compact, local-first "catalog" idea for surface-level metadata about user sessions (snapshots, checkpoints, annotations) so clients can discover, estimate cost/latency, and choose to restore/stream without forcing full payload downloads.

Motivation / why this feels useful:
- Many desktop/edge clients want to present a list of past conversations/contexts without pulling whole KV blobs.
- We want a small, authenticated, privacy-aware index that can be cheaply synced and combined with server-side truth.
- Helps client prefetch decisions: warm up KV cache, pre-reserve tokens, choose model variant.

Design goals (high level):
- Compact: index entries are small (<= 1KB typical) and mostly metadata.
- Layered trust: client-visible index vs server canonical; support partial trust levels.
- Privacy-first: explicit sensitivity flag, redaction policy, retention TTL.
- Cost-aware: include heuristic cost_estimate and preferred_deployment hints.
- Extensible: arbitrary tags, feature flags, and user annotations.

Non-goals:
- Not intended to replace full archival store or conversation replay format.
- Not an authorization layer — assume existing token scopes.

API sketch (rapid):
- GET /v1/session-catalog?user_id={uid}&since={ts}&tags={csv}
  - returns list of catalog entries (small metadata). Pagination.
- GET /v1/session-catalog/{entry_id}  -> full catalog entry (still small; may include pointers to blobs)
- POST /v1/session-catalog/ingest  (client pushes a new/updated metadata entry)
- POST /v1/session-catalog/resolve/{entry_id}?mode={restore|stream|preview}  (server returns chosen restore plan)

Example catalog entry (pseudo-json; this object itself is intentionally compact):
{
  "id": "sc_9a2f3c",
  "user_id": "u_712",
  "created_at": "2026-02-28T18:12:03Z",
  "title": "Draft onboarding flow - 2026-02-28",
  "summary": "short: 3 prompts + tool-call traces, last active 2 days ago",
  "size_estimate_bytes": "48200",
  "token_estimate": "~1.2k",
  "sensitivity": "low|contains-personal-email",
  "retention_ttl_days": "90",
  "cost_estimate_cents": "15",
  "preferred_deployment": "hosted-api:stable-small-model",
  "kv_index_hash": "sha256:abc...",
  "blob_pointer": "s3://sessions/u_712/sc_9a2f3c/blob.v1",
  "tags": ["onboarding","sales-copy"],
  "client_note": "local: contains TODOs, prefer preview first"
}

Config sketch: cataloging policy (server side + client hints) - YAML-ish:
catalog.policy:
  default_ttl_days: 90
  max_index_size_bytes: 1024  # per-entry target
  privacy_levels:
    - none
    - low     # metadata only, no PII in title
    - redacted
    - sensitive
  ingestion_rules:
    - if content.flags.contains('sensitive') -> mark sensitivity: sensitive, require_kms: true
    - if user_pref.auto_archive == true -> retention_ttl_days: 365

Client-local index behavior (notes):
- Local index stores entries as compact rows; UI shows title, excerpt, last_active, token_estimate, cost_estimate.
- On open: client calls GET /v1/session-catalog?since=last_sync and merges new entries; conflict resolution: last-write-wins with vector timestamp.
- For preview: client requests resolve?mode=preview which returns a small prompt-summary and first-2 tokens sample (masked for sensitive).

Restoration plan steps (resolve API) - server returns an ordered plan of operations the client should execute to restore:
1) choose model variant (hosted/dedicated/private) based on preferred_deployment & latency hints
2) open stream to blob storage for checkpoint diffs (range requests)
3) apply client-side fast-path: incremental-kv, prewarm top N keys
4) fallback: if range fetch fails, full blob download + local decryption

ASCII diagram (very rough):
[Client UI]
   |
   |-- local_index.db (small sqlite)
   |-- prefetch planner -> calls /v1/session-catalog -> gets entries
   v
[Remote Catalog Service] -- auth --> [Object store (blobs)]
      |
      |-> catalog-policy-service (TTL, redaction)

Notes to self (fragmented):
- Think about "index obfuscation" for enterprise tenants (don't reveal title until authorized). Could return title_hint (hashed) + client-side opt-in to reveal.
- Cost estimate calibration: initially use static linear model (tokens * model_rate) + storage retrieval cost. Need telemetry to regress.
- Edge case: long-running sessions where token_estimate grows; include last_token_count and delta since last snapshot.
- Should catalog entry carry provenance chain? (which model produced summary, user-edits, tool invocations) -> add small provenance array of short tokens (no PII).

Open questions:
- Should clients be allowed to index non-owner sessions for collaboration? How to surface ACLs cheaply in catalog? (maybe entry.acl_summary: "team:read-collapsed")
- Sync semantics: do we need vector clocks or will server authoritative timestamps be sufficient? For offline-first we probably need a simple conflict strategy + tombstones.
- Encryption: if blobs are client-encrypted, we must still be able to expose a catalog entry with pointer but not leak metadata that would deanonymize. What metadata is acceptable?

Experimental ideas / cheap probes to run next sprint:
- Bake a small pilot with 10 power users: client only displays catalog entries older than 24h, measure reduction in full-blob download by %
- Add cost_estimate field and report whether users act differently when price shown (A/B).
- Try prefetch planner that reserves 50 token budget when preferred_deployment=="dedicated" to see latency improvement.

TODO (short):
- [ ] Draft proto schema for catalog entry (one page) and post to repo
- [ ] Wire a simple GET endpoint that returns synthetic entries for UI prototyping
- [ ] Add telemetry keys: catalog_sync_ms, preview_fail_count, restore_plan_time

References / quick links:
- See linked PR for minimal proto -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/catalog-proto/pull/12
- JIRA-IR-2382: privacy considerations for session metadata

End of notes.

(Keep this intentionally rough. The goal is a compact operable surface that clients can use to avoid heavy blob transfers and to be privacy-aware.)
